newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close shade low on high volumes.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close shade low on high volumes.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly lower, but turnover was boosted by foreign buying of blue chips, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 1.45 points lower at 728.00. Price declines led losses by 28 to 19. Commercial Bank fell three rupees to 202, Hayleys two to 225.
"There was some late buying which came in, probably after the index remained unmoved in the first session of trading," said Dihan Dedigama of John Keells Stock Brokers.
Colombo stocks have been range-bound since last week, when liquidity dried up after investors returned to the sidelines to see if their absence would have an impact on prices.
Turnover was 63.9 million rupees, led by foreign buying of 132,000 Ceylon Brewery, 14,500 Development Finance and 90,000 John Keells Holdings.
Brokers say buyers were willing to take substantial quantities of blue chips and other growth stocks, but a lack of sellers was holding back trading.
"Finding quantity at current price levels is like extracting water from a stone," said a broker who declined to be identified.
